Challenge in these appeals is to the orders dated 12.01.2024 and 16.02.2024 passed by the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Bench at Aurangabad, in Writ Petition No. 10012/2022 and Review Application No. 33/2024 respectively.

sentences.text: The issue before the High Court was with regard to the validity of the application filed under Order I Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, by the petitioners before it, viz., respondent Nos. 1 and 2 in these appeals.

This application was filed in connection with a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 18941, for enhancement of the compensation payable for acquisition of the land in Gat Nos. 90 and 92 situated at Village  Jalkot, Taluk  Tuljapur, District  Osmanabad,

The tussle is now amongst his sons as to who should be impleaded in the pending Reference Application.

The writ petition was disposed of by the order dated 12.01.2024, with the following observations: -

There shall be no order as to costs.
Aggrieved thereby, Review Application No. 33/2024 was filed by the appellant.
However, the said review petition came to be dismissed on 16.02.2024.
At this stage, we are informed that the only Reference Application which is under consideration before the Reference Court as regards the subject land is in the name of the appellant.

Irrespective of whether all the legal heirs of late Kerba Babaji Kadam are required to be heard by the Reference Court, the issue as to who is to be paid the enhanced compensation, if any, and in what proportion,
is not an issue that would be decided by the Reference Court under Section 18 of the 1894 Act.

After disposal of the Section 18 reference, the Reference Court would invariably have to refer the matter under Section 30 of the 1894 Act for determining the status and the apportionment of the enhanced compensation, if any, amongst the persons claiming to be entitled thereto.
Making that position clear, the appeals are disposed of.
